= SDK native account ownership

Public ClientConfig::set_native_byte_account installs a shared account in producer configuration.
Generic producer Client, BaseProducer, FutureProducer and AdminClient construction retain that account through native client destruction.
AdminClient uses the native producer type.
Consumer construction still rejects an attached account before native creation.
This ownership slice does not activate a public accounted consumer or change Connect, log or DLQ construction.

AccountedNativePtr is a passive destruction region owning one NativePtr and its optional account lease.
Its native field is destroyed before the lease field, so the existing native destructor completes while the lease is still held.
NativeClient stores its pointer and account in that owner and exposes the same borrowed account to its dependent owners.
The existing NativePtr and its pointer-array representation remain unchanged for all other native resources, including admin input arrays.
The separate accounted constructor retains a supplied Arc without reserving its capacity again.
The account remains the existing monitor whose final Rust owner waits for attached native clients and outstanding charges before releasing the caller's reservation.

Every SDK queue handle inherits the account of its originating client: the setup log queue, independent queue, main queue, consumer queue and split partition queue.
Queue polling returns an owned NativeEvent immediately, retaining the same queue account before the event leaves the poll call.
Both ordinary client event handling and the admin polling thread use this owned result.
There is no separate raw event handoff that can omit the account lease.
An empty result releases its temporary account reference without retaining an event.
The admin oneshot sender transfers the complete event owner to its receiver, including when the result outlives AdminClient.
BorrowedMessage and RetainedConsumerMessage keep their existing native-event and consumer lifetime rules.
Existing independent Metadata and ordered completion/connection account owners retain their separate destruction order.

The account lease protects the native account monitor; it does not retain the native client or authorize queue use after client destruction.
Polling and queue operations require their existing live client and callback owners.
Client teardown disables and purges the native main, consumer and partition queue owners before final client disposal.
A remaining SDK handle can then release the native queue reference without losing its account early.
The independent admin queue is destroyed before the native client after its existing polling thread has joined.
An escaped admin-result event owns its independent result payloads; event destruction frees those native result owners before returning any op charge and releasing the Rust lease.
No native client reference cycle, additional actor, task, waiter, queue, side table or stored callback is introduced.

The unexecuted SDK source fixtures enqueue an actually accounted native error op on a queue belonging to a publicly constructed accounted producer Client.
They cover independent-queue purge after client disposal, a polled charged event retained after both queue and client disposal, rejected oneshot handoff, native main-queue purge before its last handle, empty/missing queue results, denied op allocation and the legacy NULL-account profile.
The injected error op has no callback, topic, buffer or other client-dependent final destructor.
A separate actual AdminClient request times out through its real polling thread and oneshot channel, then retains the returned native event after admin/config destruction and checks final reservation release.
That admin result remains an unadmitted native output allocation; its fixture proves the existing escape edge's account lifetime.
These private SDK unit fixtures require the vendored SDK's own test target and have not been compiled or run in Phase 1.

This slice propagates lifetime authority and does not add allocation admission for SDK wrapper bookkeeping, native client/queue construction, admin results, detached outputs, native sorting internals or all native allocation classes.
Unsafe raw FFI pointers remain the unsafe caller's ownership obligation.
Public accounted consumer construction, a whole-native bound and runtime/Phase 2 verification remain separate gates.
